Mr. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Md. Monzurul Alam, Advocates ------ Opposite-party No. 2

full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan, J: Rule has been issued in this Criminal Miscellaneous Case filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.c), at the instance of the accused-petitioner, calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 5326 of 2011, arising out of C.R. Case No. 24 of 2011, under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, now pending in the Court of Joint Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to issuance of this Rule, in short, are that the complainant is a banking company and has been running it's business as per Sharia Law. The accused-petitioner is the owner of M/S. Premier Industries. On 03.07.2001 the petitioner applied to the complaint bank for loan, to run his business. Accordingly the complainant bank had sanctioned composite limit of BDT 85 lac (Bai Moyazzel), 10 lac against TR and BDT 75 lac on account of LC/MPI, vide the concerned sanction letter and -the same was scheduled to be repaid within 1 year. But the petitioner failed to repay the same within the specified period of time. Thereafter, on 27.07.2002, the petitioner applied for extension of the said composite limit and the complainant bank has extended the same, up BDT 90 lac (Bai Moyazzel), against TR, BDT 10 lac and against LC/MPI, BDT 1.80 lac. The petitioner accepted terms and conditions. But, the petitioner failed to adjust for extension of the said limit, in time the total outstanding dues, that stands at Tk. 91,58,941.27 as on 04.01.2011. For the purpose of adjustment of the said loan, the petitioner issued a cheque in favour of the complainant bank for an amount of Tk. 91,58,941.27 and the complainant presented the said cheque, on 04.01.2011, in the account of the accused-petitioner, maintained with the complainant bank. But the same was returned with the remark 'Insufficient fund' and, thereafter, on 12.01.2011, the complainant bank served a demand notice upon the petitioner, through their lawyer and the same was received by the petitioner on 17.01.2011. But he did not repay the amount due under the cheque and as such, he has committed offence under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act 1881 (N.I. Act) The petitioner, therefore, filed a complainant petition under section 138(1) whereupon C.R. Case No.24 of 2011 was registered and the Metropolitan Magistrate, by his order dated 02.03.2011 took cognizance of the offence under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, against the accused-petitioner and also issued summons against him. The accused-petitioner appeared before the Court and was enlarged on bail by order dated 03.04.2011 of the concerned Magistrate. The case being ready for trial it was sent to the Court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, received in that Court on 29.05.2011, wherein it has been registered as Metropolitan Sessions Case No.5326 of 2011. In that case, the accused-petitioner filed an application under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 15.11.2012, the date fixed for framing charge. The Court concerned having considered, the petition filed under section 265C, has most illegally, by his order dated 15.11.2012, rejected the petitioner's application filed under section 265C of Cr.P.C. and framed charge against under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, and fixed on 05.05.2013 for trial. Further case of the accused-petitioner is that the opposite party No.2, Social Islamic Bank Ltd, has also filed Artha Rin Suit No.9 of 2011 earlier, on 31.01.2011, on the self same matter for recovery of the same loan. Hence the subsequent proceedings initiated under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, amounts to be abuse of the process of the Court below. The accused-petitioner, therefore, filed moved this petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the instant Rule. 

 4. Mr. Md. Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner, having placed the petition along with materials on record, first of all submits that the Bank has filed Artha Rin Suit No.9 of 2011, on 31.01.2011, against the petitioner, before the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka praying for recovery of loan amounting to Tk. 92,18,516.27/-, along with interest and the said suit is still pending for disposal. Thereafter, the complainant hank again filed C.R. Case No.24 of 2011, under section 138(1) of the N.I. Act, before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for dishonor of a cheque No. AWCD 219515, for Tk. 91,58,941.27/-. The said cheque was drawn on 04.01.2011. The learned Advocate submits that the cheque was taken from the complainant for recovery of loan granted by a sanction letter dated 02.10.2011. As such, he continued, for recovery of the self same loan two proceedings are pending, one in the Artha Rin Court and another under section 181(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881. He also asserts that the accused-petitioner is not bound to re-pay the loan twice. Therefore filing of the subsequent proceedings under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act is clear abuse of the process of the Court below. Next, the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner has referred to a circular issued by Bangladesh Bank concerning clearance of non MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Reorganization) cheque and submits that by a circular No. DCSPS-04/10 dated 28.04.2010 it has been instructed by Bangladesh Bank that clearance of non MICR cheque will be allowed till 30.04.2011 and that time has been extended till 31.05.2010. This instruction of Bangladesh Bank was originally conveyed through DCMPS circular No.03/10, dated 11.02.2010. But the cheque referred to in the complaint petition of the Bank is a non MICR instrument and as such it has become stale and is not a valid instrument. Hence also, the impugned proceeding, based on a non MICR cheque, is liable to be quashed on this ground alone. He also submits that, existence of 3 parties are required to for a valid a cheque, namely (I) the drawer of the cheque, (2) the payee and (111) the bank on which is the cheque has been a drawn. But in the instant case the opposite party No.2 bank is the payee as well as the concerned cheque was drawn in the accounts maintained with the payee bank. Hence, the concerned cheque does not have the character of a cheque as defined in the Negotiable Instrument Act. For these reasons he has prayed that the Rule may be made absolute. 

 5. Mr. Mohamad Ali, the learned Advocate appeared for the opposite party No.2 Bank, having taken us through the petition as well as the supplementary affidavit and other materials on record, submits that the question as to whether a suit for recovery of loan or money can stand with a Criminal case tiled under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, has been set at rest by the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division has held that the Civil Suit stands for recovery of money and the Criminal case stands punishment for committing an offence alleged. As such, there is no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner on this point. As regards the decisions cited in 23 BLT (AD) 76, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2, submits that, in that case charge was framed under section 420 of the Penal Code and propriety of framing charge under section 420 was the moot in that case. In 23 BLT (AD) 76, he continues, the question as to whether a under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and a proceeding under section 138(1) can proceed together was neither agitated before nor decided by the Appellate Division. As such the ratio of 23 BLT (AD) 76 is liable to be distinguished in this case. Without disputing the genuineness of the above mentioned Bangladesh Bank Circular, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No.2 submits that, the aforesaid DCSPS circulars contains instructions of Bangladesh Bank, addressed to the scheduled banks only, whereby by Bangladesh Bank has required the schedule banks to replace the non MICR cheques and to procure cheque books from the customs of the bank by issuing MICR cheque books. The aforesaid circulars were neither addressed to, nor binding upon the payee of the non MICR cheques houses. Moreover, this circular of Bangladesh Bank was purported only to regulate Dhaka clearing house. These circulars were not intended to deprive the payee of a cheque or the holder of a cheque in due course. Hence, the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, as regards the purpose of these circulars, is totally misconceived as well as contrary to law. He further argued that, it is the date appearing on the face of the cheque, not the date of handing over the cheque, what is the material consideration under the proviso to section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act. The learned Advocate further submits that, in the instant case, the 3 parties namely (I) the payee and (II) the bank on which the cheque is drawn are very much present. To explain, he submits that, in this case the accused petitioner is the drawer, the SIBL is the payee, so far the cheque has been drawn in it's favour, on account's maintained with the SIBL Bank. The complainant/payee bank is the also the banker of the drawer. As such he continues, the SIBL represents the character of the payee and also the character of the banker of the drawer. SIBL acted here in two distinct capacities. Hence the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner on this point is misleading and misconceived, he asserts. He concludes that this Rule has no merit. Hence, it is liable to be discharged with cost. 

 7. To address the issue as to whether a Civil Suit for recovery of money or the Artha Rin Suit can stand along with a Criminal Case initiated under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Acts, we have consulted the case reported in 17 BLC (AD) 177 for answer. In that case it has been held by the Apex Court that, "sub section (1) of section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act has not made any qualification of the cheque so returned and either post dated given as security for repayment of the loan availed by a loanee, as alleged by the accused, or any other cheque issued by the drawer for encashment currently". In 49 DLR (AD) 132, in 63 DLR (AD) 79 and in 17 BLC (AD) (167), it has been consistently held that both civil suit for recovery of money and a Criminal case can stand together and that pendency of Civil Suit on the self same matter is no legal impediment in filing a Criminal case. Hence, the law is settle that the Artha Rin Suit and Criminal case filed under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act can proceed simultaneously. 

 8. We have taken next, for consideration, the submission made on behalf of the accused-petitioner, relying upon the decision reported in 23 BLT (AD) 76. We find that, in that case the propriety of the framing charge under section 420 of the Penal Code vis-a-vis a normal banking transaction was decided by us our Apex Court. No charge was framed under section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, in the case considered in 23 BLT (AD) 76, nor any question as to whether an Artha Rin Suit can proceed along with a case filed under Negotiable Instrument Act was either agitated before, or decided by the Appellate Division in 23 BLT (AD). As such, we are of the opinion that, the case reported in 23 BLT (AD) 76 is liable to be distinguished in the facts and circumstances the case before us. 

 18. In view of the facts and circumstances of this case and having consulted the law and the decisions cited above, we do not find any merit in this Rule. Hence, the Rule is liable to be discharged.
